title: Viewer: keep the camera over the cells; cap the zoom past the fit
body:
## Summary

Zooming in toward a blank part of the 2-D embedding left the plot empty and black. The camera target could leave the cells, and the zoom could go six levels past the fit. Two changes:

```diff
 Scatter (onViewStateChange)
+  target = clampTarget(target, box)   box = the cells' box (blended during the morph; per pane when split)
 maxZoom
-  fit + 6
+  fit + MAX_ZOOM_PAST_FIT (4)
```

The first fix on its own still left the view black at the cap, because the corners of the cells' bounding box are empty. The zoom cap is what keeps a cell in view.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on the dev run, scroll-zoom at a blank point above the trajectory, 15 ticks. The plot went black, and the URL target sat at (-0.13, -0.63), away from the cells. Nothing drew, and the console showed no error.
  **After:** the same zoom leaves the target at the edge of the cells' box, and at the cap the plot still shows the green and blue clusters.
- `make web-ci` exit 0: lint, typecheck, 67 unit tests (new: `clampTarget` keeps the target inside the box on x and y and leaves z alone), build.
- `make web-e2e` exit 0 (1 test).
- 3-D view checked by hand after the change: cells still draw.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Front-end only, two constants and one helper; reverting restores the old camera behaviour. The camera state is kept in the store, so the change does not affect saved views in the URL.

**Blast Radius:** small

- Pan and zoom are clamped to the cells' box, so a user cannot pan past the edge of the plot. This is intended, but it changes how panning feels at the edges.
- The zoom cap is now four levels past the fit instead of six, so very close views of a single cell are no longer reachable.
- Split view: each pane clamps to its own cells.

title: Web run form: terminal names and method parameters
body:
Closes open-work item 3 in `docs/HANDOFF.md`: the web app can now set terminal states and method parameters when it starts a run. The API, the engine and `lumencell run` already accepted both; this PR adds the form.

![The run step on the NHL-6 dataset: the terminal picker, the parameter form drawn from the PAGA + DPT schema (N Dcs set to 8), and Run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shreyandhawa/lumenCell_V2/pivot/70-run-inputs/docs/images/run-inputs-form.png)

## What it does

- **Parameters** are drawn from each method's JSON Schema (`/methods`) by a small renderer in `ParamForm.tsx`: integers, numbers, strings, enums, and an optional value written `anyOf [T, null]` (empty sends `null`, the method's own rule). No new dependency.
- **Defaults** come from the schema. Each method's entries are kept while you switch between methods.
- **Invalid values** (out of range, fractions for integers, non-numbers, values not in an enum) show under the field and block Run.
- **Server validation errors** (`invalid_params`) show under the field they name; any other error is listed in the alert.
- **Terminal states** are ticked from the labels of the method's `cluster_key` column, the labels the dataset has. Leave them unticked and the method finds the terminals itself. A method without a `cluster_key` gets no picker.
- The request sends every parameter, defaults included. The server fills defaults the same way, so the run id is the same as a run with defaults.

## Tests

- `ParamForm.test.tsx`, `TerminalPicker.test.tsx`: defaults, ranges, nullable fields, enums, the request shape, field errors.
- `App.test.tsx`: a run with a changed parameter and a terminal (the request body is checked), an out-of-range value that blocks Run, and a server validation error shown under its field.
- `e2e/slice.spec.ts`: the run step sets `N Dcs` to 8 and checks the POST body before the lineages are checked.
- `make ci` exits 0 on this branch.

## Notes

- `HANDOFF.md`'s deviation about run inputs is updated. The reference-score deviation is untouched; the trust-panel work is in another session.
- The renderer covers only the types the current schemas use. A new kind (boolean, nested object) would render as a number box, so extend `ParamForm.tsx` before a method uses one.

title: Show reference benchmark results in the trust panel
body:
Fills the trust panel's **Reference results** section with each method's published benchmark results. Closes the empty `reference_scores` gap from the council review.

## What the panel shows
- One row per dataset and gate: the score, the threshold exactly as in `benchmarks/thresholds.toml`, Pass / Fail / Not measured, and a detail line (for example "worst case; fails 3 of 12 cases").
- Failures are shown. Unmeasured gates are shown as not measured, never as a pass.
- A line states these are the method's reference results, not a score for the user's data. Each dataset group names its source file and commit.
- Scores are rounded down, so a value under its bound never reads as the bound.

![Reference results in the Evidence panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shreyandhawa/lumenCell_V2/pivot/71-reference-scores/docs/images/trust-panel-reference.png)

## How it is built
- `src/lumencell/bench/reference.py` reads `benchmarks/baseline.json` (synthetic) and the latest `real-*.json`, and writes one small generated file, `src/lumencell/bench/reference_scores.json`. Pass or fail is decided by the existing `check_gates`.
- `reference_data.rows_for(method)` reads that file. It imports only the standard library, so an installed wheel can read it.
- `MethodInfo.reference_scores` is now a list of `ReferenceRow`, filled per method by the server. The panel reads it from `/methods` for the run's method. OpenAPI and TS types regenerated with `make contract`.

## Tests
- `tests/unit/test_reference_scores.py`: the packaged file matches what the generator builds from the committed results (drift check); failures are kept; synthetic failing-case counts; no-gated-lineage datasets are never a pass.
- `tests/api/test_routes.py::test_methods`: the server returns the rows.
- `tests/test_wheel.py`: a wheel built from this branch, installed into a fresh venv with no dependencies, reads the rows.
- `ReferenceResults.test.tsx` and `App.test.tsx`: grouping, status text, floored scores, unmeasured rows, empty state.

## Not in this PR
- The run step (`MethodRunner`) is untouched.
- The thresholds and results are unchanged.

## Discrepancies with `docs/HANDOFF.md`
The committed numbers and the handoff disagree in two places. The panel shows the committed numbers:
- **Palantir on bone marrow passes** in `real-2026-11-20.json` (branch accuracy 0.943 against 0.75; all three gates pass). The handoff's failure came from the 2026-11-10 run (0.639).
- **PAGA+DPT fails 9 of 12 synthetic cases** (any gate), per the generated `docs/benchmarks.md`. The handoff's "7" is stale.
- Palantir on bone marrow is the handoff's example of a failure. It is not a failure in the committed latest result, so the panel shows it passing.

title: 3-D viewer, phase 8: share and export, version 0.3.0
body:
## Summary

Phase 8, the last of the 3-D viewer overhaul, stacked on #71: share a view, export it, tour it. Version 0.3.0.

```diff
 App
   useDefaults()
+  useSharedView()                    after the defaults, so a link's choices win
+    once the dataset and runs load:  decodeView(location.hash, dataset.fingerprint) -> stores
+    then, at most every 300 ms:      history.replaceState(#encodeView(view on screen))
+ lib/viewUrl.ts                      v=1 & data=<fingerprint> & view & run & color & cam.<id> & focus & t & axes & size
+                                     every field checked; a bad one is dropped, another dataset's link ignored;
+                                     the selection is never stored
 state/camera.ts
+  arrival                            a link's 3-D camera: the opening morph flies there instead of the default tilt
 <Scatter> controls
+  [Export PNG]  lib/exportPng.ts     deck.redraw() -> the plot area cut from the canvas on the stage colour,
+                                     plus caption, root pin, legend, gimbal and a provenance line
+  [Camera tour] CameraTour.tsx       save up to 8 views of the 3-D stage, go to one, or play through them
+                                     (linear between views); moving the view yourself stops it
 GET /dataset
+  fingerprint                        the file identity runs already record; the link names it
 version 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0 · README: three new screenshots · HANDOFF: the overhaul, its PRs, merge order, gotchas
```

A shared link looks like this (NHL-6, 3-D on DC1, DC2, DC4, Cluster 7 focused):

```text
#v=1&data=9d2734919f5bc8dc719fee76&view=3d&run=b4ddf7a74597d3f1&color=obs%3Alumencell_leiden
 &cam.stage=0.1503%2C-0.0371%2C-0.2332%2C9.2327%2C18%2C-48&focus=1&axes=1%2C2%2C4
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** there was no way to show someone else what you were looking at, short of a screenshot, and no image export with its provenance.
  **After:** on Sheih NHL-6 (21,762 cells):
  - **The link in a new tab** opens 3-D on DC1, DC2, DC4 with Cluster 7 focused. The camera is identical: the gimbal's line ends match to the last digit (`20.0739…, 0, −22.2943…`).
  - **The same link with another fingerprint** opens the default 2-D view and rewrites the address.
  - **Export PNG** downloads `lumencell-nhl6-3d.png`, 72 KB and a valid PNG. It has the caption, the root pin and label, the Leiden legend, the DC1/DC2/DC4 gimbal and "lumenCell 0.2.0 · nhl6 · 9d27… · Palantir (experimental) · run b4dd… · 2026-11-21". The line names the server's version, and that dev server was started before the bump to 0.3.0.
  - **Camera tour:** saving a view, turning away and choosing "Go to view 1" restores it exactly. Play is off under reduced motion, like auto-rotate.
  - No console errors.

Tests:

```text
lib/viewUrl.test     round trip; defaults left out (a plain view is "v=1&data=…&view=2d");
                     another dataset, another version or no hash -> null;
                     bad fields dropped: view=4d, run=../etc, color=obs:, a 5-number camera, focus=-1, t=7,
                     axes=1,1,2, size=40
api/test_routes      /dataset carries the file's fingerprint
e2e step 7           Camera tour: save, turn, "Go to view 1" -> the gimbal is back; Play disabled (reduced motion)
e2e step 11          Export PNG -> the download starts with the PNG signature
e2e step 12          3-D + z = DC4 -> the hash has axes=1,2,4 -> reload -> 3-D, "DC1, DC2 and DC4",
                     the focused lineage and the same cursor are back
```

`make ci` is green on the commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed! · no issues found in 78 source files
py-test                  1449 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  66 passed (4 new)
web-e2e                  1 passed
```

### Decisions

- **A bug the link found:** the 2-D ↔ 3-D morph could start before the 2-D embedding had loaded. It then did nothing, and ran again later with the default tilt. The morph now waits until the stage has its first camera, and runs again when it does. The bug also affected opening straight into 3-D.
- **Only the shown view's cameras are stored** (`stage`, or `flat` and `deep` side by side), rounded to 4 decimals. The theme stays a personal setting and is not in the link.
- **The colour-by codec moved** from the sidebar into `state/ui.ts` (`colorByKey`, `parseColorBy`), so the menu and the link write the same strings.
- **The PNG is drawn, not screenshotted.** The legend, pin and gimbal are DOM on screen, so `exportPng` draws its own versions on a 2-D canvas, with no new dependency.
- **Not built:** saved views in the link, video export, and the selection in the link (by design).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Frontend, plus one new field on `/dataset`. A revert removes the hash, the buttons and the field; links made meanwhile then open the default view.

**Blast Radius:** stage

The address bar now changes as you use the app (`replaceState`, so the back button is unaffected). `DatasetInfo.fingerprint` is required in the generated TypeScript type, so hand-built fixtures must set it; the one fixture does.

title: 3-D viewer, phase 7: graph overlays and 3-D axes
body:
## Summary

Phase 7 of the 3-D viewer overhaul, stacked on #70: the graph overlays and the 3-D axis picker. It needs phase 5's API (#69), so phase 5's commit is cherry-picked onto this branch. Merge #69 first: once it is on `main`, rebasing this stack drops the copy, because the patch is identical.

```diff
 Display options (the sliders button)
   Point size · Fade far cells in depth
+  3-D axes      x [DC1] y [DC2] z [DC3]       choosing one already shown swaps the two axes
+  Graphs drawn over this view
+    [ ] PAGA cluster graph                    GET /graph/paga?embedding=<this view>
+    [ ] Neighbour graph                       GET /graph/knn (a seeded sample above 50,000 edges)
+    "Both are built from neighbours in PCA space. A line joins where its ends sit in this view,
+     so its length means nothing."
 <Scatter>
-  useEmbedding("dc123") · useCurves(run, "dc123")
+  useEmbedding(axesName(axes)) · useCurves(run, axesName(axes))   dc123, or dc:i,j,k
+    the last coordinates stay up until the new ones arrive (keepPreviousData); the GPU
+    moves the cells to the new axes like the 2-D <-> 3-D morph
   scene(prefix, tt, positions)
     halo
+    neighbour graph   LineLayer, binary line ends per view, faint, under the cells, morphs with them
     cells
+    PAGA              clusters at the mean of their cells (placed through the morph like milestones),
+                      edge width and opacity by connectivity; hover: "Cluster <id> · <n> cells · PAGA"
     curves, milestones, playhead
   caption, gimbal                               DC1, DC2, DC4 · 3 of 14 diffusion components
 <TrustPanel> curve fidelity                    on the chosen axes too
 App: the default embedding is picked from the 2-D ones only (dc123 is listed since #69)
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** the 3-D view was always DC1–DC3. The PAGA graph and the neighbour graph that inference reads were never drawn.
  **After:** on Sheih NHL-6 (21,762 cells, the Palantir run):
  - Setting z to DC4 relabels the caption ("DC1, DC2, DC4 · 3 of 14 diffusion components") and the gimbal, and moves the curve fidelity to those axes. Cluster 7 is drawn with fidelity 0.94 there, against 0.60 on DC1–DC3. Choosing DC1 for z swaps it with x.
  - PAGA draws 10 clusters and 29 edges over UMAP, over DC1–DC3 and in both split panes.
  - The neighbour graph draws 50,000 of 494,546 edges, and the panel says so.
  - Morphing 2-D → 3-D with both graphs on, and switching to DC5, gave no console errors or warnings.
  - Each graph is fetched once: `paga?embedding=umap`, `paga?embedding=dc123`, `knn`.

Tests:

```text
lib/axes.test     dc123 for DC1-DC3, dc:1,2,4 otherwise; labels; choosing a shown component swaps axes
lib/graph.test    each edge's ends land on its two cells
e2e step 2        before a run: "DC1–DC3 · 3 of N diffusion components"
e2e step 7        z = DC4 -> caption and gimbal "DC1, DC2 and DC4"; DC3 restores them;
                  both graph checkboxes fetch /graph/paga and /graph/knn with 200, no console error
```

`make ci` is green on the commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed! · no issues found in 78 source files
py-test                  1449 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  62 passed (3 new)
web-e2e                  1 passed
```

### Decisions

- **The caption counts the components there are to choose from** ("3 of 14"), not the ones inference used. Before a run it said "the first 3". The Evidence sheet still says how many components inference used.
- **The neighbour graph sits under the cells.** It shows in the gaps, where its long-range edges are, and does not haze over the clusters. Its line ends are built once per view and kept per positions buffer, so the 2-D ↔ 3-D morph moves them on the GPU with the cells.
- **A disabled TanStack query keeps its cached data,** so the overlay reads the toggle too. Without that check, unticking the neighbour graph left it drawn.
- **Not built:** hiding edges to cells past the pseudotime cursor, PAGA's tree-only edges, and a choice of axes for the 2-D view.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Frontend, plus phase 5's backend copied from #69. Both overlays are off by default, and the axes start at DC1–DC3, so nothing changes until the user asks. Nothing is stored.

**Blast Radius:** stage

The 3-D caption text changed (it now says "3 of N diffusion components" before a run too). `useEmbedding` keeps the previous coordinates while a new name loads, for every embedding, so a future 2-D embedding picker would show the old embedding until the new one arrives rather than a blank stage. The curve-fidelity row now wraps on narrow sheets when the axes are not DC1–DC3.

title: 3-D viewer, phase 6: linked split view
body:
## Summary

Phase 6 of the 3-D viewer overhaul, stacked on #68: the 2-D embedding and DC1–DC3 side by side, linked. Frontend only.

```diff
 state/ui.ts
-  view: "2d" | "3d"
+  view: "2d" | "3d" | "split"
 <Scatter>
   [2-D] [3-D]
+  [Split]                                  enabled once DC1-DC3 has loaded, like 3-D
   <DeckGL>
-    views = stage                          one OrbitView, morphing 2-D <-> 3-D
+    views = split ? [flat, deep] : stage   two OrbitViews in one canvas, each half the free stage
+    viewState = split ? {flat, deep}       a camera per pane in the camera store, fitted per pane
+    layerFilter                            "flat:*" layers draw only in flat, "deep:*" only in deep
-    layers = cells + trajectory at t
+    layers = scene("", t) | scene("flat:", 0) + scene("deep:", 1)
+    onHover -> hovered                     the hovered cell is ringed in both panes
+  controllers                              only the pane the pointer was over last gets keys
+  lasso                                    takes cells in the pane it starts in (its own projection)
+  root pin in each pane, label once · divider · a caption per pane
```

Shared between the panes: colouring, selection, pseudotime cursor and playhead, focused lineage (focusing one turns the 3-D pane around it), the hovered cell, and Reset (both panes). Auto-rotate and the gimbal belong to the 3-D pane. The single stage keeps its own camera, so leaving the split view returns to it, morph included.

## Evidence

- **Before:** you could see the 2-D embedding or DC1–DC3, never both, and comparing them meant morphing back and forth.
  **After:** on Sheih NHL-6 (21,762 cells, the Palantir run):
  - Hovering a cell in UMAP rings the same cell in DC1–DC3.
  - Shift+arrows with the pointer over the UMAP pane leave the 3-D pane alone; over the 3-D pane they turn it, and R restores it.
  - A lasso in the UMAP pane takes 11,322 cells (Clusters 1, 2, 4 whole); a lasso on the 3-D arm takes 12,476. Each lights up in both panes.
  - Both themes work, and there are no console errors.
- **Frame times at 100k cells** (synthetic, Apple M4, headless Chromium on Metal, 3 s each):

  ```text
                         orbit drag          hover sweep
  single 3-D             60 fps, p95 16.7    60 fps, p95 16.7
  split                  60 fps, p95 16.7    52 fps, p95 33.4
  ```

title: 3-D viewer, phase 5: graph and axes API
body:
## Summary

Phase 5 of the 3-D viewer overhaul: the backend that phase 7's overlays and axis picker will draw from. Backend only, from `main`, independent of the frontend stack (#65 → #68).

```diff
 GET /dataset
   embeddings
     dc12        dims 2
+    dc123       dims 3                  listed now (it was served but hidden)
+    components  n diffusion components  diffusion views only, for the axis picker
 GET /embeddings/{name}
-  dc12 | dc123                          two hard-coded branches
+  dc12 | dc123 | dc:i,j | dc:i,j,k      one parser; components differ and run 1..n, else 404
 GET /trajectories/{id}/curves?embedding=
+  any of the names above                kept in a 16-entry LRU per (run, embedding)
+GET /graph/paga?embedding=              Leiden centroids on that view + PAGA's weighted edges (JSON)
+GET /graph/knn?max_edges=50000          LCB1 src u32 · dst u32 · w f32, each edge once (src < dst);
+                                          above the cap a seeded uniform sample, meta total_edges / sampled / seed
```

The fidelity warning now names the axes it was measured on, and its hint fits the view:

```diff
-On the dc123 embedding, lineage 'Cluster 7' is drawn with fidelity 0.74: ... Try the diffusion (DC) view.
+On DC1, DC2 and DC3, lineage 'Cluster 7' is drawn with fidelity 0.74: ... Try other diffusion components.
```

Both graphs are dataset-level drawings of prep's own graphs (the kNN connectivities and PAGA over `lumencell_leiden`), so they live under `/graph`, not under a run. Nothing here runs inference on a display embedding: the embedding only places the nodes.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `/dataset` on NHL-6 listed `umap, dc12`. Any 3-D view other than DC1–DC3 was a 404, and there was no graph route. Curves were projected again on every request (about 40 ms each).
  **After:** on Sheih NHL-6 (21,762 cells):

  ```text
  /dataset                      umap (2), dc12 (2, 14 components), dc123 (3, 14 components)
  /graph/paga?embedding=umap    10 nodes, 29 edges, 2.4 KB, 2 ms
  /graph/knn                    50,000 of 494,546 edges, sampled, 600 KB, 13 ms
  /graph/knn?max_edges=500000   all 494,546 edges, 5.9 MB, 12 ms
  /embeddings/dc:1,2,4          200 · /embeddings/dc:1,1  404
  curves paga_dpt dc:1,2,4      40 ms, then 1 ms from the cache
  ```

Tests:

```text
unit/test_projection        dc12 · dc123 · dc:1,2,4 · dc:3,1 parse; dc:1 · dc:1,2,3,4 · dc:0,1 · dc:01,2 · "dc:1, 2" do not;
                            the warning reads "On DC1, DC2 and DC4," on a diffusion view, "On the noise embedding," otherwise
unit/test_graph_payloads    PAGA nodes at the mean of their finite cells; a cluster with none is left out with its edges;
                            3-D sets z; each kNN edge once (one-sided entries and self-loops handled);
                            the sample is a subset, the same for the same seed, different for another
api/test_routes             graph routes are 409 before prep; dc123 listed with dims 3 and components;
                            dc:1,2,4 equals diffmap[:, [1, 2, 4]]; 8 bad names are 404;
                            PAGA centroid equals the UMAP mean of cluster 0, edges = upper-triangle nnz;
                            kNN weights equal connectivities[src, dst], max_edges 0 and 500,001 are 422;
                            curves on dc:1,2,4 have 3-D points and milestone z, and a repeat does not project again
api/test_contract           both graph routes declared; /graph/knn advertises LCB1
```

`make ci` is green on the commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed! · no issues found
py-test                  1449 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  36 passed
web-e2e                  1 passed
```

### Decisions

- **`components` on `Embedding`:** the axis picker in phase 7 needs to know how many components it can offer, and nothing in `/dataset` said so. It is null for non-diffusion views.
- **A uniform sample, not the strongest edges.** Keeping the strongest edges would crowd dense regions. A seeded uniform sample keeps the graph's density honest, and the same request always draws the same edges.
- **404 for a malformed or out-of-range `dc:` name,** matching any unknown embedding. The message gives the valid range.
- **The heatmap cache and the new curves cache share one helper** (`_remember`), so the LRU logic is written once.
- **Not built:** PAGA's spanning-tree flag on edges, and a server-side cache of kNN payloads (the route takes 13 ms).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive routes and fields. A revert removes them. Nothing is stored.

**Blast Radius:** API

`Embedding` gains a field that is required in the generated TypeScript type (`components: number | null`), so any hand-built `Embedding` in TS must set it; the one fixture is updated. `/dataset` now lists `dc123`, so a client that took every listed embedding as 2-D would read 3 columns as 2. The frontend on `main` only reads names, and phase 7 filters on `dims === 2`. The fidelity warning text changed for diffusion views; nothing parses it.

title: 3-D viewer, phase 4: lasso selection in 2-D and 3-D
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 of the 3-D viewer overhaul, stacked on #67: selecting cells, in 2-D and 3-D. Frontend only.

```diff
 <Scatter>
+  [Lasso select] tool                   left drag draws; the event is stopped in the capture phase, so
+                                          deck.gl never sees it; right drag, wheel and keys still move the view
+  lasso -> projectAll(xyz, pixelProjectionMatrix) -> selectInPolygon -> combine(mask, next, op)
+  Alt-click -> deck.pickObject -> every cell in the clicked cell's group (shown colouring, lineage or Leiden)
+  Esc clears
   cells layer
+    getSelected (float per cell, stepMode dynamic)
+    DepthFadeExtension: unselected -> 80% toward the stage, half size, behind every selected cell
+                        selected   -> full colour, no fog
+    halo off while a selection exists (it would ring every shrunk cell)
+  <SelectionBar>                          count and share · New/Add/Subtract/Intersect · Clear
+                                          top groups: share of the selection · share of each group taken
 state/selection.ts                        mask (1 byte per cell), count, op
 lib/selection.ts                          projectAll, combine, countSelected, composition (pure, tested)
```

A 3-D lasso takes every drawn cell inside it at any depth, as Cellucid and Cirrocumulus do. You narrow it the Cellucid way: turn the view, choose Intersect, and lasso again. Cells hidden by the pseudotime cursor are not drawn, so a lasso never takes them. The selection is per cell, so it carries across 2-D and 3-D.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no selection of any kind. `lib/geometry.selectInPolygon` existed but nothing called it.
  **After:** on NHL-6 in 3-D, a lasso on the left arm selects 1,991 cells (9.1%: Cluster 6 62%, Cluster 3 38%). Turning the view 60° with Shift+arrows and intersecting with a tighter lasso leaves 759. Alt-clicking the root cell with Add takes all of Cluster 8 ("100% of it"), for 2,018. Switching to 2-D shows the same cells lit, and Esc clears. No console errors.
- **Pixel check of the dimming:** with every cell grey, a lasso around one area keeps the bright pixels inside it (75 → 74) while bright pixels outside drop from 4,677 to 1,441. Selecting all 21,762 cells leaves the picture exactly as with no selection (mean 353, 47,620 vs 47,621 lit pixels).

Tests:

```text
lib/selection.test.ts    projectAll matches deck.gl's viewport.project on a tilted, padded orbit view; NaN for no position;
                         new/add/subtract/intersect, from nothing too; counts and composition
lib/gl/depthFade.test    the uniform block guard now covers `dim`; the selection attribute is declared per instance
e2e step 7               Lasso select -> drag around the plot -> "N cells selected" -> Esc -> "No cells selected"
```

`make ci` is green on the commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed! · no issues found in 78 source files
py-test                  1426 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  59 passed (6 new)
web-e2e                  1 passed
```

### Decisions

- **A bug worth recording:** an attribute added by a deck.gl extension defaults to one value per *vertex*. On an instanced layer, every cell read the selection of cells 0–3, so the whole plot dimmed or didn't depending on the first four cells. `stepMode: "dynamic"` (one value per instance) fixes it, and a unit test pins it.
- **Unselected cells drop behind selected ones** (clip z pushed to the far plane). In 2-D every cell has the same depth, so the last drawn would otherwise cover a selected cell. In 3-D, selected cells inside the cloud show through.
- **The composition summary sits on the plot, not the sidebar.** The plan put it in the sidebar, but the sidebar's Inspect step opens only after a run, while selection works before one.
- **Not built:** lasso-as-root (no such root kind, and resolving one would pick a cell the user did not choose), undo, and sphere or box selectors.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Frontend only. A revert removes the tool and the bar. Nothing about a selection is stored on the server.

**Blast Radius:** stage

While a selection exists, the faint ghost of cells past the pseudotime cursor is off, so during playback those cells disappear instead of showing as ghosts. In lasso mode a left drag no longer pans or orbits; the right drag does, and only in 3-D.

title: 3-D viewer, phase 3: the trajectory in 3-D
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the 3-D viewer overhaul, stacked on #66: the trajectory itself in 3-D. Milestones, curves that stay readable inside the cloud, a pseudotime playhead, per-curve fidelity in the Evidence sheet, and Palantir's fate entropy as a colouring. Frontend only; the API already served all of it.

```diff
 <Scatter>
   halo, cells
-  curves     PathLayer, depthCompare "always"
+  trajectoryLayers()                     components/scatter/trajectoryLayers.ts
+    curves-behind  on top, faint         the stretches inside or behind cells (focused lineage: full, magenta)
+    curves         depth-tested, full    the stretches in front
+    travelled      on top, magenta 5 px  focused curve from the root to the playhead
+    playhead       on top, magenta dot   where the focused lineage's cells are at the cursor
+    milestones     on top, pickable      forks = rings, tips = dots (the root keeps its pin)
+  3-D: focusing a lineage turns the camera around its curve (450 ms)
+  tooltip: cell -> "<shown value> · pseudotime 0.43 · Cluster 6"; milestone -> "End of Cluster 6 · pseudotime 0.96" / "Fork · …"
 <TrustPanel>
+  Curve fidelity: per lineage, "<2-D embedding> 0.88 · DC1–DC3 0.86"
 Colour by
+  Fate entropy                            only when the run serves extras.entropy (Palantir)
```

Binned curves follow the mean position of their cells, so they run through the middle of each cloud. With a plain depth test they would mostly vanish in 3-D, so each curve is drawn twice. The faint pass on top shows where a curve goes behind cells.

`lib/trajectory.ts` holds the geometry, pure and tested:

```text
placeMilestones(run.milestones, 2-D positions, 3-D positions, mix)   # joins kind/label onto projected positions, mid-morph too
cursorPoint(pseudotime, lineage membership, xyz, cursor, ±0.02)      # mean of the lineage's cells near the cursor, or null
prefixTo(curve, point)                                               # the curve up to its vertex nearest the point, then the point
centroid(curve)                                                      # the camera's new target on focus
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** in 3-D the curves sat on top of every cell, with no depth. Milestones and per-curve fidelity were fetched but never shown, and the tooltip gave only the shown colour's value.
  **After:** on NHL-6 (PAGA + DPT, root `timepoint = IP`), with Cluster 6 focused in 3-D, its curve is magenta from the root through the fork to its tip, and the camera centres on it. At pseudotime 0.92 the travelled stretch and playhead sit where Cluster 6's cells are. Hovering the root cell reads "Cluster 8 · pseudotime 0.08 · shared trunk". No console errors.
- The Evidence sheet now shows what the drawing can hide. On NHL-6:

```text
Cluster 7   umap 0.74 · DC1–DC3 0.58
Cluster 2   umap 0.49 · DC1–DC3 0.75
Cluster 6   umap 0.88 · DC1–DC3 0.86
```

Cluster 7's curve in DC1–DC3 starts and ends 0.016 apart, next to the root, so it shows as a short magenta stub there. That is the projection, not a drawing fault: its DC1–DC3 fidelity is 0.58.

Tests:

```text
lib/trajectory.test.ts   8 new: milestone mixing and fallback, cursor point (lineage only, gaps, NaN), prefix, centroid
App.test.tsx             curves handler echoes ?embedding=; the trust test checks the Curve fidelity rows
                         (lineage names now appear twice, so the lineage lookup is scoped to the Lineages list)
e2e step 5               Curve fidelity shows "DC1–DC3 <number>" for the real run
```

`make ci` is green on the commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed! · no issues found in 78 source files
py-test                  1426 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  53 passed (8 new)
web-e2e                  1 passed
```

### Decisions

- **The playhead follows the focused lineage only**, and only where that lineage has cells within ±0.02 of the cursor. In a gap (NHL-6's pseudotime is bimodal) there is no playhead rather than a guessed one.
- **Camera turns on focus in 3-D only.** In 2-D, clicking a lineage in the list does not pan the plot.
- **Milestone wording** follows the run's kinds: forks and tips. The root milestone is not drawn, since the root pin marks the root cell. `cluster` milestones are not drawn.
- **Entropy colouring** was checked on a Palantir run of NHL-6. "Fate entropy" appears in Colour by only for that run. The legend reads "fate entropy (Palantir) 0.0772 – 0.712" and a cell reads "fate entropy 0.10 · pseudotime 0.11 · shared trunk". Entropy is low at the root and the tips and rises along the arms. It reads one optional array from the same `/cells` payload and uses the existing viridis and robust-domain helpers.
- **Not done:** the plan's "hover a heatmap column moves the marker". The heatmap view was removed in #63; the gene trends already share the cursor, which moves the playhead.

Frontend only. A revert restores the curves-on-top drawing and removes the new section and option.

**Blast Radius:** stage and Evidence sheet

title: 3-D viewer, phase 2: GPU morph, 3-D before a run, keyboard and auto-rotate
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the 3-D viewer overhaul, stacked on #65: the 2-D ↔ 3-D morph runs on the GPU, 3-D opens as soon as preparation is done, and the plot has keyboard controls and auto-rotate. Frontend only.

```diff
 view switch
-  every frame: lerp all n cells in JS -> new Float32Array -> upload
+  once: layer data points at the other embedding's attribute object
+        deck.gl transitions.getPosition interpolates on the GPU (600 ms, same cubic-bezier as the camera)
   every frame: camera, fog strength, curves and root pin follow t (as before)
```

```diff
 <Scatter>
-  useEmbedding(runId ? "dc123" : null)                     # 3-D waited for a finished run
+  useEmbedding(prep ready ? "dc123" : null)                 # 3-D right after preparation; click-a-cell root works in it
   <DeckGL
+    onLoad -> name the focusable plot: role="application", label lists the keys
     controller
-      2-D  { dragMode: "pan", dragRotate: false }
+      2-D  { dragMode: "pan", dragRotate: false, keyboard: { rotateSpeedX: 0, rotateSpeedY: 0 } }
       3-D  { dragMode: "rotate" }                           # arrows pan, -/= zoom, Shift+arrows orbit
+  onKeyDown: R resets the view (not while typing in a field)
+  [Auto-rotate]  3-D only, 12°/s; a drag, R, reset or view switch stops it; disabled under reduced motion
```

The position attribute objects are memoised per embedding. deck.gl starts a transition when that object changes, so a recolour (which rebuilds the layer data) never restarts the morph.

## Evidence

- **Before:** 3-D was disabled until a run finished. The morph allocated and uploaded a new n × 3 buffer every frame for 0.6 s. There were no keyboard controls.
  **After:** on NHL-6, frames captured inside the page at fixed times show the cells between shapes at 210, 310 and 410 ms. The root pin moves continuously along the same curve (y = 294 → 305 → 348 → 399 → 410 px), so the pin and the GPU stay together. Auto-rotate turns the gimbal and reports `aria-pressed="true"`. No console errors.

New e2e checks:

```text

step 7  focus the plot (role application) -> Shift+ArrowLeft -> gimbal changes -> R -> gimbal back to the tilted preset
        Auto-rotate is disabled (the suite runs with reducedMotion: "reduce")
```

title: 3-D viewer, phase 1: real depth, GPU fog, world-size points
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the 3-D viewer overhaul: real depth, fog on the GPU, and points that face the camera. Frontend only, no API change.

```diff
 <Scatter> (web/src/components/Scatter.tsx)
   halo     ScatterplotLayer   drawn first, no depth: the ghost of cells past the cursor
-  cells    ScatterplotLayer   depthCompare "always", pixel radius, flat disks
-           + per-frame JS pass: view depth for every cell -> new colour buffer -> alpha fade
+  cells    ScatterplotLayer   depth test + write, billboard, radius in embedding units
+           extensions [DataFilter (cursor), DepthFade]
   curves   PathLayer          + billboard
+  Display options             point size 0.5-3x, "Fade far cells in depth"
```

`DepthFadeExtension` (`lib/gl/depthFade.ts`) runs in the vertex shader:

```text
colour.rgb = mix(stage, colour.rgb, colour.a)   # alpha keeps its meaning (missing, shared trunk)
colour.a   = 1                                  # opaque, so the depth buffer works
t          = (distance(cell, camera) - near) / (far - near)
colour.rgb = mix(colour.rgb, stage, 0.6 * t)    # fog; 0 in 2-D and during the morph's start
fragment:  discard if alpha < 0.5               # antialiased rims would punch holes in cells behind
```

`near` and `far` are the camera's distances to the closest point and the farthest corner of the box that holds the cells, computed once per draw from 8 numbers. The fade runs before the picking highlight, so a hovered cell is never fogged. The stage colour follows the theme.

```diff
 web/src/
 ├── components/
 │   ├── Scatter.tsx               # 483 -> 457 lines
+│   └── scatter/{Gimbal.tsx, useStageSize.ts}
 ├── lib/
+│   ├── camera.ts                 # Camera, FLAT/TILTED, lerpCam, fitZoom, depthRange
+│   ├── embedding.ts              # normalise as one flat loop, + bounds
+│   └── gl/depthFade.ts           # the extension and its shader module
 └── state/
+    ├── camera.ts                 # camera per view id (split view and URL state need it later)
     └── ui.ts                     # + pointSize, fog
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** 3-D cells drawn in data order (`depthCompare: "always"`), so a far cell drawn later covered a near one, and hover picked by draw order. Depth came only from alpha, recomputed in JS for all n cells on every camera frame. Points were disks in the XY plane that went edge-on as you orbited.
  **After:** on Sheih 2020 patient NHL-6 (21,762 cells, root `timepoint = IP`, PAGA + DPT), near clusters cover far ones, the far arms fade, and turning the fog off restores full colour. Checked at 1440×900 in both themes, 2-D and 3-D, with no console errors. Screenshots are in the session's scratchpad (`phase1/`), not committed.

Scale, on a 100,000-cell synthetic file in headless Chromium on the real GPU (Apple M4, Metal, 2880×1800 canvas), orbiting for 3 s:

```text
after    60 fps · p50 16.7 ms · p95 16.7 ms · worst 16.8 ms · no page errors
removed  the per-frame fade pass: 0.22 ms JS + 391 KB colour upload at 100k
                                  2.17 ms JS + 3.9 MB upload at 1M (node, JIT warm)
```

So at 100k this is not a visible speedup. The win is correct depth and picking, and per-frame cost that no longer grows with the cell count.

`make ci` is green on the commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed!
py-test                  1426 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  45 passed (9 new: normalise, camera, depthFade uniform block + draw)
web-e2e                  1 passed
```

New e2e checks in step 7: the 3-D canvas has drawn pixels (`expect.poll(drawnShare) > 0.001`, so a shader that fails to compile or draws nothing fails), and "Fade far cells in depth" removes "far cells fade" from the caption.

A guard test asserts the shader's uniform block fields match `uniformTypes` in order and type, since std140 offsets follow that order and a mismatch fails silently on the GPU.

### Decisions

- **Fog fades colour, not opacity** (as Cellucid and Cirrocumulus do). Cells stay opaque and pickable.
- **Fog strength 0.6**, fitted to the cells' box rather than a bounding sphere. The sphere left elongated clouds dimmed even at the front. Trade-off: fog darkens the far half of a pseudotime cloud, so yellow reads as olive there. The toggle is the way out.
- **Point size** is in embedding units, so it matches today's pixel size at the fitted zoom, grows when zooming in, and is clamped to 0.6–3× before perspective. In 3-D, near cells look bigger.
- **Halo kept**, drawn first without depth, because it is how cells past the pseudotime cursor stay visible.
- **e2e lookups are exact** for Play, Pause, 2-D and 3-D. Playwright matches names by substring, and "Display options" contains "Play".
- 3-D still opens only after a run; that changes in phase 2.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Frontend only. A revert restores the old rendering. No API, contract or stored data changes.

**Blast Radius:** stage

Every cell on the plot now renders opaque, in 2-D too, so dense 2-D regions look more solid than before (overlaps no longer add up). Missing values still read as faint. Circle edges are hard-thresholded, so very small points rely on the browser's MSAA for smooth edges.

```text
  <Sidebar>        steps rail               Step x4: PrepProgress · RootPicker · MethodRunner · Colour by + LineageTree
  timeline         bottom, one cursor       <GenePanel> (gene trends, opens on play/scrub) + <PseudotimeBar>
  <TrustPanel>     Evidence sheet           verdict · checks · clones against nulls · provenance · warnings
```

API: the 3-D stage reads DC1–DC3 from `GET /embeddings/dc123` and the tree from `GET /trajectories/{id}/curves?embedding=dc123`.

```diff
 class LineageCurve(Model):
-    points: list[tuple[float, float]]
+    points: list[tuple[float, ...]]   # two coordinates; three on dc123
 class MilestonePosition(Model):
     x: float
     y: float
+    z: float | None = None            # set on dc123
```

`dataset_view.embedding("dc123")` returns `diffmap[:, 1:4]`, and `project()` keeps up to three columns. `dc123` is not added to the `embeddings` list, because it is not a 2-D display embedding and `tests/api/test_routes.py` pins that list. The client was regenerated with `make contract`.

Motion, all through `motion`:

| What | Trigger | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| 2-D ↔ 3-D morph (positions and camera together) | switch | 600 ms, ease-in-out |
| Pseudotime washes out from the root, once | run goes queued/running → done | 900 ms, ease-out |
| Evidence sheet in/out, stage re-centres | toggle or a run arriving | 240 ms in / 160 ms out, ease-out |
| Gene trends in/out | play or scrub | 200 / 150 ms, ease-out |
| Root pin appears; reset view; button press | root set; reset; press | 200 / 300 / 160 ms, ease-out |
| Playback | play | linear, 8 s for 0 → 1 |

With `prefers-reduced-motion`, the morph and reset jump, the wash is skipped, and motion components keep only their fades. Playback still runs, because the user asks for it.

## Evidence

**Before:** the three-column app (header, sidebar, scatter, gene panel, trajectory panel).
**After:** `make ci` is green on the final commit:

```text
py-lint / py-typecheck   All checks passed! · Success: no issues found
py-test                  1426 passed, 43 deselected
contract-check           API contract is up to date
web lint · types · test  36 passed
web-e2e                  1 passed (slice.spec.ts, reducedMotion: "reduce")
```

### Screenshot comparison

All six states were captured at 1440×900 with headless Chromium on the real Sheih 2020 patient NHL-6 file. It was split with the case study's own `split_units`, and the declared clone settings (`clone_id`, `patient`, strata `timepoint`) and root `timepoint = IP` were used. The run reproduces the recorded result the mockup's Evidence values came from: weak, C1 1.00 ≥ 0.95, C2 0.795 left out, C5 p 0.000999 with Δη −0.008, η 0.415 / 0.103 / 0.089 against N1 / N2 / N3, k-means 0.422, and 548 clones (58.8 effective). Those numbers match the frames exactly. The point clouds and gene trends in the frames were synthetic, so the clouds differ.

| Frame | Matches | Differs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Prepare (running) | Rail and step states, stage list with done/running, "N of M" aside, background hint, disabled bar "Pseudotime appears after a run", 3-D locked | This file stores no UMAP, so the stage says "No embedding yet: preparation will compute one." instead of showing a stored X_umap. Prep has a 9th stage, Cell cycle ("4 of 9"). |
| 2 Pick a root | Chosen card with ✓, root pin and label "Root · timepoint = IP", Run step "ready" with the Experimental mark and the magenta Run button, Leiden legend chip, caption "umap · coloured by Leiden cluster" | The card text is the server's resolution rule (the frame's "Stored in the file …" was mock text). An "Other starts" ghost button reopens the choices. A reset button is shown in 2-D. Cluster 0 is blue, not orange (see the palette decision). |
| 3 Run finished, 2-D | Done steps with asides, Inspect with Colour by and the lineages, the whole Evidence sheet verbatim (label, "A real failure, not a cap…", C1–C5 values and lines, null line, η rows, provenance), viridis bar with ticks and "pt 0.00" | Real pseudotime is bimodal: the infusion product is purple and post-infusion cells are near 1. PAGA + DPT curves are binned projections, not a clean fitted tree. Lineage names are auto names (Cluster 7 / 2 / 6). A gene search sits under Colour by. A Warnings section follows Provenance (scroll). |
| 4 3-D, Evidence open, weak | Caption "DC1–DC3 · 3 of N diffusion components · far cells fade", focused lineage in magenta on the stage and in the rail, gimbal with DC1–DC3 labels, reset, Evidence as in 3 | It reads "3 of 10" and "X_diffmap, 10 components", which is the run's `n_dcs`; the frame says 15. The DC geometry is the real one. |
| 5 Playback with gene trends | Header "GENE TRENDS · ALL LINEAGES · SAME AXIS AS THE BAR", one cursor from the handle above the trends through the bar, "pt 0.55", cells past the cursor keep only their halo | The genes are the run's top temporal genes (GBP6, COL5A2, AC069…, AC139…), not the mock's CCR7 / PDCD1 / MKI67 / GZMB. Trend lines break where a pseudotime bin holds no cells. The capture scrubbed with the keyboard, so the bar shows its focus ring and the Play icon rather than Pause. |
| 6 Light, 3-D | Light tokens, amber `#B07A00` mark, light gimbal, magenta focused lineage, sun toggle | As in 4 |

The six PNGs are in the session notes folder, `track3b-explorer-screenshots/`.

### Decisions

- **One `OrbitView` for both views.** 2-D is the camera looking straight down at z = 0. Both embeddings are centred and scaled into a unit box, so positions and camera morph together on the CPU (lerp per frame). The data is centred between the rails with the view's `padding`.
- **Far cells fade in 3-D.** Each cell's view-space depth is read from the viewport's view matrix, and alpha falls to 25% at the far end.
- **Halo.** A separate faint neutral disc layer sits under the cells (white 10 / 255 dark, black 14 / 255 light). Cells past the cursor or the wash keep only their halo. The cursor and the wash use `DataFilterExtension` on pseudotime.
- **The wash** runs only when the active run goes from queued or running to done in this session. Reloading a finished run does not replay it.
- **Gene trends** open when the user plays or scrubs. Genes are the ones the user picked (gene search under Colour by), then the run's top temporal genes for the focused lineage, or the first lineage (heatmap endpoint, top 4). There is one line per lineage, the focused one in the accent. The value shown is the focused lineage's, or the mean of the lineage trends at the cursor, with a tooltip that says so.
- **Evidence sheet.**
  - The per-check lines are plain words derived from each check's state and values. The API's full reasons are in tooltips.
  - The verdict always uses the amber mark, because no served level is a positive verdict.
  - `LEVEL_LABEL` is unchanged from main, so `supported` still reads "Not shown to be a tree".
  - I added a Warnings section after Provenance. It is not in the frames, but curve-fidelity and run warnings are trust information the old panel showed.
- **Pick a root.**
  - There is no obs-names endpoint, so clicking a cell starts from that cell's cluster in the shown colouring. The copy reads "Or click a cell to start from its cluster" (the frame said "Or click a cell on the stage").
  - On NHL-6 the suggestions offer d12 and a heuristic cluster, never the declared `timepoint = IP`. Canvas clicks are not keyboard-accessible either. So I kept the old column + value picker, restyled: "Or choose a cluster" with a secondary "Start here". Once a root is chosen, the choices close behind "Other starts" so the Run step stays in view, as in frame 2.
- **Removed from the UI, API routes kept:** lasso selection and its summary, run list and run comparison, pseudotime window filter, the top-temporal-genes heatmap view, lineage rename, the embedding picker and the header. The 2-D view uses the dataset's default embedding.
- **Reset view** is also shown in 2-D. The frames show it only in 3-D, but without it a panned-away 2-D view has no way back.
- **The gimbal** is a small SVG built from the view matrix, with DC labels. `@deck.gl/widgets` was not needed (its gimbal has no axis labels), so the only new dependencies are `motion` and the two `@fontsource-variable` Atkinson Hyperlegible packages (Next and Mono, OFL-1.1), bundled into the wheel's `web_dist` by Vite.
- **Palette.** Okabe-Ito without reddish purple and without black (the stage). `#0072B2` stays first because `lib.test.ts` pins it, so cluster 0 is blue where the mock showed orange. The extension colours are reordered to differ from the first six, with pinks and magentas removed.
- **Amber** appears only in the mark (experimental, provisional, weak). Errors and notices use ink-coloured icons. The run-progress bar is ink, not accent.
- **Trust polling.** `useRun` polls every 2 s while clonal scoring, stability or any check is pending, so the verdict updates without a reload.
- **Timeline columns.** The gene-name column is 52 px (the frame has about 40) so seven-character genes fit, which puts the track at x = 380 instead of 362. The scrubber is a native range input with an invisible thumb, widened by half a thumb at each end so click travel matches the track. The cursor line is the visible cursor.
- **Captions.** In 2-D: "{embedding} · curves are projections of the tree inferred in {inference_rep}". PAGA + DPT curves are binned, not fitted, so "fitted in diffusion space" would be wrong.
- **The theme toggle** is not remembered across reloads.
- **Tests.** The Playwright test is rewritten for the new interface with `reducedMotion: "reduce"`. `App.test.tsx` also had to change for `make ci` to stay green: the same six tests and intents, with selectors and words updated to the new UI. No tests were added.
- **No threshold, recorded number or verdict rule changed.** `docs/superpowers/HANDOFF.md` is untouched, as in #61 and #62.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A revert restores the old interface. The API change is additive: curve points widen from 2-tuples to 2- or 3-tuples, and milestone positions gain an optional `z`. 2-D callers get the same JSON.

**Blast Radius:** UI-wide

The whole web interface is replaced. Anyone relying on the removed UI features (lasso, run comparison, pseudotime window, heatmap view, lineage rename) loses them in the browser, though their API routes remain. The 3-D view needs WebGL. It was checked at 1440×900 only, not at small widths.

title: Build the Daniel 2022 dataset: join contigs to cells by capture and call clones
body:
Phase 3 Task 5b: `build` and `BUILD_VERSION = 1` for Daniel 2022.

For each listed capture, the builder joins that capture's contigs to its own cells (a contig barcode `b` is the matrix cell `tag + b`), calls clones with `call_clones` and writes one `.h5ad` by atomic rename.

**Freeze:** the builder has not been run on the real files, and no real file was opened. The tests use the synthetic layout in `tests/unit/daniel_fixture.py` only. No clone x state, clone x capture or clone x lineage count was computed.

What it does:
- **Cells:** `obs_names` are `<gsm>_<core>`, where the core is the 16 nt without `-1`. A capture keeps the matrix barcodes `tag + [ACGT]{16} + "-1"` that its own matrix's metadata lists. The metadata index is the matrix barcode itself, so cells match by exact string.
- **D5:** each capture is read only from the matrix its `Capture.matrix` names, so the D5 copies of the main captures are never read and nothing is deduplicated. If both matrices are used, their features must be identical, or the build stops with `BuildError`.
- **obs:** `capture`, `arm`, `day`, `tissue`, `sort_gate`, `state` (from `LABEL_COLUMN`), `donor`, plus the `call_clones` columns (NaN, or 0 for the counts, when a cell has no contig). Of the metadata, only the index and the label column are read.
- **`uns["lumencell_build"]`:** the plan's keys and no others. A join miss is a barcode with at least one qualifying contig that matches no kept cell of its own capture. `ignored_members` lists tar members that belong to no capture. A name that does not match `SAFE_NAME` is stored as `<unsafe member name>`.
- **Params:** a bad value is refused with an error that gives counts only and never echoes it.

Tests: the plan's three verbatim tests and the listed ones, plus:
- kept-cell order and the obs and uns values
- D5 versus main reads
- mismatched features
- a features file with two columns
- a failed build leaving nothing behind
- `LABEL_COLUMN = None`

`make ci` exit 0.

Decisions are in HANDOFF, "Phase 3 Task 5b decisions".

title: Declare the case-study clone definition, namespace, strata and root before any analysis
body:
Phase 3 Task 10. This declares the Sheih 2020 case study (`[case_study.sheih2020]` in `benchmarks/thresholds.toml`) before any analysis. It was written from the paper and Task 9's note on the file headers. Nothing was downloaded, and nothing was computed from clonotype, CDR3 or gene values. It must merge before Task 11 fetches the data.

## Declared values

- `root = "cluster:timepoint=IP"`: the paper names no differentiation root (its Monocle 3 trajectory covers infusion-product cells only and found no clear trajectories). It treats the infusion product as the source of the in vivo repertoire (Results, "Contribution of infused CAR-T clusters to in vivo repertoire", Fig. 7). That is also the plan's fallback, the earliest sample. `IP` is GEO's "time point" spelling, and every patient has it. Task 11 writes obs `timepoint` with GEO's values as written.
- `chains = "paired"`: the tables are labelled "unpaired" (one row per clonotype x chain), but every row names its chain and lists its cells' barcodes, so TRA and TRB group by cell barcode, which is the plan's test for paired. The cost is that a cell with only one chain detected gets no clone label.

- **Refusals happen before any work.** `resolve_root` refuses a scoring-only `ClusterRoot` before its existence check. `run_method` checks the method's `cluster_key` and the label key it will use before resolving the root.
- **Provenance.** `TrajectoryResult.obs_keys` is the sorted set of columns that steered the run: the resolved root's `cluster_key`, the method's `cluster_key` and the label key used.
- **Store version 2.** `result.json` gains `prep_key`, `inference_isolation` and `obs_keys`. `load` restores `obs_keys` (`[]` when the key is absent), and runs saved at version 1 are left out of the list. Because `STORE_VERSION` is hashed into the run id, every run id changes.

A scoring-only one gets a 422 with code `scoring_only_column` and `detail.columns`. `models.py` and `web/` are unchanged, because error codes are free strings.

## Controller rulings applied

1. **Wording (F24).** One helper serves both engine and API. A column matching the pattern "holds clone or receptor data". A column scoring-only only because the caller named it "is set as a clone or donor column". Both wordings are tested.
2. **Roles and order.** The roles are "root column", "cluster column" and "label column". `create_run` checks the root, then `cluster_key`, then the label key. The message describes the first offender, and `detail.columns` names each offender once, in that order.
3. **`clonal_columns` is required (F4).** It has no default. If the key is missing, or is anything but a list of names, the job fails with a message naming the key. The only submitter, `api/runs.py`, sends it, and `tests/unit/test_jobs.py` now sends it too.
4. **Check order.** `run_method` checks the cluster and label columns before `resolve_root` and `impl.run`. A test makes `resolve_root` fail if it is ever reached. `obs_keys` holds only non-empty keys.
5. **No API field.** `models.py` and `web/` are untouched.

## Tests

With the exclusion off, the PCA differs (the teeth test). The file also covers the nine receptor column names, named columns, label detection, both wordings, the refusals and `obs_keys`.

title: Add the clonal package: clone codes, scores against three nulls, a k-means baseline and coupling
body:
Phase 1 Task 2. This adds `src/lumencell/clonal/`, the pure package that scores a run's lineages against T-cell receptor clones. The benchmark (oracle-cells mode) and the worker job (own-cells mode) will both call it in later tasks. It imports only numpy, scipy, pandas and `lumencell.trust.constants`.

## What changed

- `clonal/labels.py`: `is_missing`, `CloneCodes` and `encode_clones`. A clone is the pair (donor, label), so the same label in two donors counts as two clones. A labelled cell with a missing donor is dropped and counted, never pooled into a "nan" donor. Strata codes combine donor with each strata value, and a missing value gets a level of its own. Labels are compared as whole Python strings.
- `clonal/scores.py`: `score_clonal`, `baseline_space` and `kmeans_partition`, built on the definitions declared in `benchmarks/thresholds.toml` `[clonal]`:
  - normalised clone entropy, purity, clone-weighted purity, and purity without the largest clone (on a size tie, the purer clone is left out)
  - the effective clone count
  - η and p against N1 (donor), N2 (donor × pseudotime decile by average rank, with cells lacking pseudotime in a bin of their own) and N3 (declared strata)
  - the headline p, which is the largest of the null p values
  - η_base, Δη and a paired p for Δη over the same N1 shuffles
  - raw-count cosine coupling with z, p and Benjamini–Hochberg p_adj
- The shuffle is the plan's own: one generator per null, one random key per scored cell in original order, and ids permuted within strata by `lexsort((u, g))`. Shuffles are scored in blocks, and a block draws from the same random stream as one-by-one draws would.
- Undefined values are NaN and never stand in for a significant result. η is NaN when its null mean is 0. `p_delta` is NaN whenever Δη is NaN. A coupling pair with an empty lineage has NaN fields and is left out of the BH adjustment.
- The status is `single_lineage` when L < 2, or when the scored cells' mass falls in fewer than two lineages. Until now, a run with every scored cell in one lineage read as perfect agreement. Under `single_lineage` the counts and the effective clone count are reported, every other float is NaN, and nulls and coupling are empty. With no scored clone the status stays `too_few_clones`.
- `clonal/__init__.py` cites all seven sources. `scores.py` cites each one where it is used.
- `docs/superpowers/HANDOFF.md`: current state, this task's decisions, and one open question for sign-off. Spec §4.5 says scores are "unchanged" when cells are reordered, but with this shuffle that holds exactly only for the deterministic fields. The null-based fields move within Monte Carlo error.

## Why

Clones are evidence that the inference never sees. This package turns that evidence into a score with nulls and a baseline that uses no lineages, so a run's lineages can be checked without ground truth.

## Tests

- `tests/clonal/test_labels.py`: 11 tests.
- `tests/clonal/test_scores.py`: 37 tests, hand-computed. They cover:
  - enumerated null means and p
  - entropy normalised by log L at L = 3
  - fractional oracle counts and oracle coupling
  - the NaN pseudotime stratum, and the N1, N2 and N3 strata
  - each null's random stream, reproduced by a literal loop at three block sizes
  - the single-lineage rule in both modes
  - the F6 constant baseline
- `tests/clonal/test_properties.py`: 6 Hypothesis properties, 30 examples each, B = 499.
- `uv run pytest tests/clonal -q -W error`: 54 passed in about 2 s, with no warnings. The reordering and singleton properties keep only cases with at least two clones and computed nulls, and the reordering property is derandomised so its Monte Carlo bound is checked on the same examples every run. Each property also passed at 400 examples locally.
- Seeded bugs were each caught: p without the +1, NaN pseudotime merged into decile 0, a reversed tie-break, `p_delta` on NaN, N1 ignoring donor, oracle cells in no lineage, a random stream that depends on unscored cells, shuffles across strata, log 2 in place of log L, 1/2 in place of 1/L, N3 by donor only or across all cells, N2 without donor, shared or unseeded null streams, the old single-lineage rule, a NaN effective clone count, and a wrong JMLR volume.
- `make ci`: exit 0. 430 Python tests passed and 12 were deselected; 36 web tests and 1 end-to-end test passed.

title: Stop leaking the job worker when launch is stopped
body:
## Summary

When `lumencell launch` was stopped with SIGTERM (`kill <pid>`, or `proc.terminate()` in `test_server.py`), its job worker and resource tracker kept running for ever, with parent PID 1. Every pytest run added another pair.

**1. SIGTERM now runs the job manager's shutdown.**

```diff
 launch
+  SIGTERM handler: raise SystemExit(128 + 15)
   try
     uvicorn.run(...)    # catches SIGTERM, shuts down, re-raises it under the previous handler
   finally
+    restore the previous SIGTERM handler   # a second SIGTERM ends it at once
     jobs.shutdown()     # was skipped: Python's default handler ended the process first
```

**2. The worker now exits by itself when its parent dies.**

```diff
 worker_main
+  thread: multiprocessing.parent_process().join(); os._exit(1)
   while True
     task = tasks.get()  # blocked for ever before: the worker holds a write end of this queue
```

Why this shape:
- **A signal handler instead of a lifespan hook.** It is a few lines in `launch` and leaves `build_app` and `create_app` alone. uvicorn already restores that handler and re-raises the signal under it. SIGINT already unwound, as KeyboardInterrupt.
- **SIGHUP is not handled.** uvicorn doesn't catch it, so a handler fires inside the running event loop, cancels uvicorn mid-flight and prints a lifespan traceback. A server stopped with SIGHUP (or SIGKILL) dies outright, and change 2 then ends its worker.
- **The worker blocks on `parent_process().join()` instead of polling `os.getppid()`.** That needs no timer. `os._exit` ends the worker mid-job too, since numba or igraph code can't be interrupted any other way.

## Evidence

`tests/api/test_server.py::test_stopping_launch_stops_its_job_worker[SIGTERM|SIGKILL]` launches the server and lists its children by PID. It then sends the signal, checks the exit code, and polls for up to 10 s for children that are still running.

- **Before:** `AssertionError: still running after the server stopped: {… resource_tracker …, … spawn_main(…) --multiprocessing-fork}`. The SIGTERM case failed on origin/main, and the SIGKILL case failed with only the first commit.
  **After:** both cases pass. The SIGTERM case exits with 143. If the handler is removed, it fails on the exit code (-15) even though change 2 is in place.
- `make py-ci contract-check` exits 0 at each commit (254 tests passed, then 255), and `make ci` exits 0 on the last commit.
- The test helper now also kills any child that outlives the server, so a failing run leaves no processes behind.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** shutdown

- On SIGTERM, `launch` now exits with code 143 instead of being killed by the signal (-15). A supervisor that counts "killed by SIGTERM" as clean but exit code 143 as a failure would notice. Nothing in this repo checks it.
- `jobs.shutdown()` still waits up to 5 s for a busy worker, so SIGTERM during prep takes about 5 s to exit, as Ctrl+C already did.
- No conflict with #1: `git merge-tree` of the two branches is clean, and this PR doesn't touch `jobs/manager.py`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way, with one exception.

Every cache change is additive: a dataset name in the manifest and a `last-used`
stamp file. Old caches load and list. The exception is root text: after this
merge, a root whose name the plain form can't carry is saved as `json:{...}`. If
the merge is reverted, the old parser refuses those saved roots, so the app shows
no root until one is picked again. `cache prune` deletes data by design, but only
when a user runs it.

**Blast Radius:** backend

The server now loads the dataset without its matrix, so any future server code
that needs it gets a clear `DatasetError` instead. A job running past 3 h is now
stopped. The new workflow runs on every pull request.
